header.name: Titan Company Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Titan Company (NSE: TITAN), part of the Tata Group, sells jewellery, watches and eyecare products; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹87,584 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹20,614 crore, 10.1% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 13.2% against 9.0%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹2,393 crore, 113.7% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 6 Nov 2026, the first session after the result, TITAN shares rose 3.42% while the NIFTY 50 rose 2.01% and the NIFTY CONSUMER DURABLES index rose 1.70%; allowing for the market's move, TITAN's own move was +1.28%, about 1.06 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the consumer durables sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹4,910 (NSE close, 16 Nov 2026), the reinvestment-phase discounted cash flow model (Template B, since TITAN's median return on invested capital of 26.7% is above its 11.21% cost of capital) matches the price if revenue grows about 44.7% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 8.6%; TITAN's revenue grew 32.1% a year over FY22–FY26.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: In Titan's own cash-flow statement the largest working-capital movement in FY25 and FY26 is the increase in inventories, part of it matched by more gold on loan, which the company shows within operating activities; the template counts the rest of that inventory build as reinvestment.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to the operating margin (two percentage points either way: a model value of ₹1,716 to ₹3,572 a share) and to the cost of capital (one percentage point either way: a model value of ₹2,068 to ₹3,459 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹1 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, plus investments in joint ventures and associates, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹4k crore of cash and treasury.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY22–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY22 to FY26.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of TITAN's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.what: Revenue grows at 50% of its FY22-FY26 rate for five years, the operating margin slips 2 points, and growth after year 10 earns no more than its cost of capital.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.what: Revenue keeps its FY22-FY26 growth rate for five years, the FY26 margin holds, and TITAN keeps its historical return on capital indefinitely.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.what: Revenue grows 2 points a year faster than its FY22-FY26 rate for five years and the margin rises 1 point.

valuation.rule_note: The cost of debt and long-run growth are set by fixed rules and not reviewed by a person.

template_b.name: Template B · reinvestment phase
template_b.why: Template A needs free cash flow to the firm to be positive in at least three of the last four years, and here it was ₹496 crore in FY23, −₹35 crore in FY24, −₹1,630 crore in FY25 and ₹1,804 crore in FY26.
template_b.test: Template B runs the same model but asks a different question of the past: does the capital being reinvested earn more than it costs? The median return on invested capital over FY24–FY26 was 26.7%, against a cost of capital of 11.21%. Its bear and bull cases are set around the history growth rate, because the latest years are the reinvestment itself.
tiles: economic profit after year 10, today's value
template_b.first_positive: In the base case, free cash flow turns positive in FY33: until then the growth is paid for by reinvestment, while economic profit is already positive.

flags.title: Gold on loan is treated as an operating liability
flags.text: Titan's gold on loan is gold borrowed from banks and printed as a financial liability apart from borrowings. It is treated as an operating liability because the cash-flow statement shows its changes within operating activities. Counted as debt instead, invested capital would be higher and free cash flow lower in the years it grew.

flags.title: The reinvestment version of the model is used
flags.text: Template A did not apply (free cash flow not positive in at least 3 of the last 4 years), so this page uses Template B, which is judged on return on capital and assumes today's return on capital lasts.

flags.title: The exchange's files contain errors
flags.text: 24 reconciliation checks fail on the exchange's own files, each with a recorded reason. They are marked as explained, not passed, and the figure as filed is used, never a corrected one.

limitations: Template B (reinvestment phase): the same single-stage fade model, judged on return on capital rather than past free cash flow. The base case assumes today's return on capital lasts; no currency driver.
Cash flows are discounted to the balance-sheet date, 30 Sep 2026, two months before the price date; the model does not roll that gap forward, so its values are slightly low against the price.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.

Gold on loan (gold borrowed from banks, printed as a financial liability apart from borrowings) is treated as an operating liability, because Titan's cash-flow statement shows its changes within operating activities; it is not counted as debt. Counted as debt, invested capital would be higher by its balance and free cash flow lower in the years it grew.
Non-current investments are treated as non-operating, like cash, and so leave invested capital.

From FY23 the figures come from the exchange XBRL filings; the FY22 balance sheet and the FY23–FY26 lease and gold-on-loan lines come from the results PDFs (scanned pages, read from their text layer and checked against the printed subtotals and the XBRL).
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
